# 4 Ezra Chapter 15 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 15:8 — "hold my peace" vs. "stay silent"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "I-will-hold-my-peace-no-more" | Literal — tacebam |
| LOGOS | "I will hold my peace no more" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "I will no longer stay silent" | More natural modern phrasing |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** "I will hold my peace no more" (LOGOS). "Hold my peace" is an established idiom that preserves the solemnity of the divine speech.

---

## 15:30 — "dragons of Arabia"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-nations-of-the-dragons-of-Arabia" | Literal — dracones Arabiae |
| LOGOS | "the nations of the dragons of Arabia" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "The dragon nations of Arabia" | Compressed |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** "The nations of the dragons of Arabia" (LOGOS). "Nations of the dragons" preserves the unusual genitive construction of the Latin.

---

## 15:37 — "dung of men unto the camel's hough"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "dung-of-men-unto-the-camel's-hough" | Literal, archaic "hough" (hock) |
| LOGOS | "dung of men unto the camel's hough" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "filth of battle reaching as high as a camel's knee" | "Knee" for "hough"; "filth of battle" for "dung of men" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** "Dung of men unto the camel's hough" (LOGOS/EMET). The grotesque literalness is intentional in this apocalyptic passage; "hough" (hock/hamstring) is a legitimate English term.

---

## 15:45 — the great eastern dragon

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-great-strong-dragon...with-a-flaming-fire-shall-he-lead-them" | Literal |
| LOGOS | "the great strong dragon...with a flaming fire shall he lead them" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "the great powerful dragon, coming in the fury of his spirit, leading with a wall of flame" | "Wall of flame" expands "flaming fire" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** "The great strong dragon, for he shall come in the fury of his spirit, and with a flaming fire shall he lead them" (LOGOS). "Wall of flame" is PNEUMA's expansion not warranted by the Latin.

---

## 15:53 — the righteous escape like clouds

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "shall-escape-like-clouds-driven-before-wind-and-hail" | Literal |
| LOGOS | "shall escape like clouds driven before wind and hail" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "they will escape like clouds driven by wind and hail" | Minor variation |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** "Shall escape like clouds driven before wind and hail" (LOGOS). "Before wind and hail" is slightly more precise than "by wind and hail" for the preposition.

---

## Total disagreements: 5
